clue.text: Old man who spoons sweetly?

parts.note: an older man who woos (spoons) a young partner and keeps things sweet with lavish gifts, the spooning pun suggesting sugar

explanation.surface: An elderly fellow romancing someone with tender kisses.
explanation.definitionFit: An older wealthy man who lavishes gifts on a young lover is a stock idiom for this kind of benefactor.

clue.text: Poetic gem's about to be replaced by a different one

indicators.note: to be replaced by tells us one part of the gem is swapped out for something else

parts.note: a sapphire is a blue precious stone
re means about or concerning
c, for circa, is another word for about

explanation.surface: A verse jewel whose setting is being changed for another stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Both RE and C mean 'about'; swapping the one for the other turns SAPPHIRE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to Sappho, the Greek lyric poet, or to the metre she used, so the adjective describes poetic form.

clue.text: Working has stopped for inspection

parts.note: a machine that is going is working
something that is over has stopped or ended

explanation.surface: Production halted so that an official check could take place.
explanation.definitionFit: A going-over is a thorough examination or check of something, an informal word for an inspection.

clue.text: Beat some good athletes, and kept inside track in this style for record perhaps

indicators.note: kept inside says one word is held within the other pieces

parts.note: rhythm is the beat of music
Blues are Oxford or Cambridge sportsmen who have represented their university
taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner beat top athletes and stayed on the inside of the track to set a record.
explanation.walkthrough: The athletics surface misleads: 'Beat', 'track' and 'record' are all musical. A Blue is a sporting award at Oxford or Cambridge universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhythm and blues is a genre of popular music in which records are made, so it is a recording style.

clue.text: Vicious raider capturing island community up north

indicators.note: capturing means the scrambled word holds another piece inside it
vicious suggests the letters of the raider are savaged and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A savage marauder seizing an island settlement in the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vicious' rearranges RAIDER into AIRDRE, and 'capturing' puts I inside it. Airdrie is a town in Lanarkshire, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Airdrie is a Scottish town, so it is a community in the north of Britain.

clue.text: Call city accent finally — this?

parts.note: to dial is to call on the telephone
EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word accent

explanation.surface: Asking whether a city's particular way of talking counts as a form of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a regional accent and speech of a city is exactly this.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional form of a language, with its own accent and vocabulary, is what a city's way of speaking is.

clue.text: One whose nemesis was white king

definitions.meaning: the captain in Melville's Moby-Dick, destroyed by the white whale
the wicked king of Israel, husband of Jezebel, in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A monarch brought down by a white rival.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to Melville's obsessed sea captain and to a biblical king of Israel.

clue.text: Army captures one group of flags

indicators.note: captures means the army surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a host is an army or a great multitude
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Troops seize a unit's set of banners.
explanation.walkthrough: A hoist is a set of signal flags run up together.
explanation.definitionFit: In naval signalling a hoist is a set of flags raised together on one line.

clue.text: Cup Final perhaps the aim of African sportsmen

definitions.meaning: a major sporting fixture is a big match
large animals such as lions and elephants are hunted on safari

explanation.surface: African players hoping to reach a showpiece match.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both an important match and the large animals pursued by hunters.

clue.text: Reporting landlord that goes over enclosure

parts.note: a journalist covering a story is reporting it
a letter is one who lets property

explanation.surface: A news story about a property owner who builds over a fenced area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enclosure' suggests a fenced field but means something enclosed with a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A note sent with a document to explain it accompanies, and lies over, the enclosure.

clue.text: John's secret

definitions.meaning: john is slang for a lavatory; the possessive reads as is
party to a secret, so private

explanation.surface: Someone's private matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an outdoor lavatory (a john) and also private or secret, as in being privy to something.

clue.text: So grannie can make such sense?

indicators.note: can make says the letters of the phrase may be reformed into something else

explanation.surface: Asking whether an elderly relative's words could add up to anything sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' rearranges SO GRANNIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Logical thought or argument is the sense of rational thinking, so the noun fits.

clue.text: The worse for drink and a drug on which one is over-assertive

parts.note: high can mean intoxicated
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Someone drunk and drugged who becomes pushy.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on this mount is an idiom for behaving arrogantly or self-righteously.

clue.text: An additional thing to remove when court leaves

indicators.note: leaves says the court abbreviation departs from the longer word

parts.note: to extract is to remove or pull out

explanation.surface: Something additional must be taken out once the judges leave.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is something added over and above the usual, an additional item.

clue.text: Worry about half a dozen initially attractive eggs that can be expensive

indicators.note: about means the worry word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: care means worry or anxiety
VI is the Roman numeral for six

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word attractive

explanation.surface: Fretting over a few eye-catching but costly eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals a container; 'eggs that can be expensive' is fish roe, and caviare is the older spelling of caviar.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviare is the salted roe of sturgeon, eggs famous for their price.

clue.text: What sets down national emblem?

parts.note: the plant that produces downy seeds, a fluffy down, and is also the floral symbol of Scotland

explanation.surface: Asking what puts a country's symbol on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sets down' reads as writing something, but it means producing down: the plant's fluffy seed heads.
explanation.definitionFit: This prickly plant is Scotland's national emblem and its seed fluff is known as down.

clue.text: Agony, endlessly sick? Try this medicinal plant

parts.note: torment is agony or great suffering

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word for sick is cut off

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: Advice to someone in pain and feeling unwell to take a herbal remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tormentil is a yellow-flowered herb of the rose family whose root was used as an astringent remedy.

clue.text: Composer of tiresome work, mostly with Wotan

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a bore is a tiresome thing or task
Wotan is the German name of the Norse god Odin

explanation.surface: A dull opera, largely about the Wagnerian god.
explanation.walkthrough: Wotan is Wagner's name for Odin, chief of the Norse gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Borodin was a Russian composer, best known for Prince Igor.

clue.text: Painter mixing blue with just enough green for one spell

indicators.note: mixing says the colours are blended into a new arrangement
just enough says only part of the colour word is used, dropping its last two letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist blending blue with a little green for a single magic touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just enough' keeps GRE from GREEN, enough to spell the name once (it has several spellings); 'mixing' rearranges BLUE with GRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieter Bruegel was a Flemish painter of peasant scenes.

clue.text: What bowler tries to hit square leg?

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three
pin is informal for a leg

explanation.surface: Asking what target a cricket bowler aims at near the square leg fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: Square leg is a cricket fielding position, but here the bowler is at a bowling alley.
explanation.definitionFit: A skittle in ninepins is the target a bowler tries to knock over.

clue.text: Crude metal fastener to hold cheque

indicators.note: to hold means the fastener goes round the other piece

parts.note: a pin is a fastener
a giro is a cheque, especially a British benefit payment

explanation.surface: Using a clip to keep a cheque in place.
explanation.walkthrough: A giro is a British government benefit cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig iron is crude iron straight from a blast furnace, before refining.

clue.text: Exercise equipment over limits of Europe where orbit's lowest

parts.note: PE stands for physical education, exercise
rig is equipment or gear

indicators.note: limits of picks the first and last letters of Europe

explanation.surface: Gym gear set above the borders of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Perigee is the point in an orbit nearest the Earth, where a satellite is at its lowest.

clue.text: Invalid act taken up in chancery till undone

indicators.note: taken up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A legal action dropped while still in the Chancery court.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'taken up' means read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A nullity is something legally void, such as an act with no legal force.

clue.text: It's up to peacekeepers to have fired back

parts.note: the UN sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: back means the word for fired is turned round

parts.note: lit means fired or ignited

explanation.surface: Deciding whether peacekeepers should return fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Until means up to a given time, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Run in credit cheat

indicators.note: in means the run letter goes inside the credit word

parts.note: tick is informal for credit
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A con man who runs up debts on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: On tick is British slang for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To trick someone is to cheat or deceive them.

clue.text: At no time shifting resistance group's transmitter

indicators.note: shifting means one letter of the word for at no time slides to a new place

parts.note: never means at no time
a cell is a small group of underground resistance fighters

explanation.surface: A resistance cell that never stays put with its radio set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' moves the final R of NEVER forward to make NERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurone carries nerve impulses, so it is a transmitter of signals.

clue.text: Spooner's Pinafore performance is subject to experiment

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: a pinny is a pinafore
a gig is a performance

explanation.surface: A production of HMS Pinafore treated as a test run.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first sounds of PINNY GIG gives GINNY PIG, said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A guinea pig is a person or thing used as the subject of an experiment.

clue.text: Expresses annoyance to one African

parts.note: tuts means clicks the tongue in disapproval
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone tutting at an African.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi, so a member is an African.

clue.text: Superior's one book dismissed by visionary engraver

indicators.note: dismissed means the book letter is sent away

parts.note: William Blake, poet and engraver of visionary works

explanation.surface: A senior figure who sacks a mystical artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' looks like a boss but is Lake Superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior is one of the Great Lakes of North America.

clue.text: Essentially where sheep congregate?

parts.note: in gives the location, where
a teg is a sheep in its second year
to rally is to gather or congregate

explanation.surface: Asking where a flock of sheep gathers.
explanation.walkthrough: A teg is a two-year-old sheep, a word mostly met in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Integrally means as an essential, built-in part, so essentially.
